title: Causal Inference for Multistate Event Processes via TMLE
text: pipeline three main steps: fit_initial() fits initial (nuisance) hazard models event process data, builds discrete product state space used internally. tmle_alpha() targets initial fit stochastic intensity intervention, scales intensity process alpha (optionally combined intervention baseline treatment). returns TMLE estimate, standard error, optionally efficient influence curve. calibrate_alpha() calibration_curve() calibrate intervention target effect size, calibrated_contrasts() decomposes total treatment effect mediated calibrated contrasts. example, simulated illness-death data illness_death, illness z raises risk death outcome1, risk death time 1 intensity illness halved estimated : simulate multistate event history data, see simevent package.
code: library(MultiStateTMLE) fit <- fit_initial(   illness_death,   fit_types = list(     z = list(       model = "Surv(tstart, tstop, delta == 2) ~ L0",       at_risk = function(dt) dt[["z"]] == 0     ),     outcome1 = "Surv(tstart, tstop, delta == 1) ~ L0 + z",     censoring = "Surv(tstart, tstop, delta == 0) ~ L0"   ),   tau = 1 )  est <- tmle_alpha(fit, target = "outcome1", alpha = 0.5, z_name = "z") est$estimate #>   tmle.est         se      g.est  #> 0.30405495 0.03853505 0.31239982

title: Calibrate an intensity intervention to a target value — calibrate_alpha
code: fit <- fit_initial(   illness_death,   fit_types = list(     z = list(       model = "Surv(tstart, tstop, delta == 2) ~ L0",       at_risk = function(dt) dt[["z"]] == 0     ),     outcome1 = "Surv(tstart, tstop, delta == 1) ~ L0 + z",     censoring = "Surv(tstart, tstop, delta == 0) ~ L0"   ),   tau = 1 )  # Risk of outcome1 under the intervention on z that brings the risk of z # down to 80% of its observed value. cal <- calibrate_alpha(fit, target = "outcome1", z_name = "z", rho = 0.8) cal$estimate #>       alpha.est        alpha.se      target.est       target.se target.se.crude  #>      0.79272380      0.00995552      0.31992034      0.03864198      0.03866085  #>           theta        theta.se  #>      0.12713026      0.02505712

code: set.seed(1405) treatment_fit <- list(estimate = c(tmle.est = 0.7), eic = rnorm(200, sd = 0.1)) placebo_fit <- list(estimate = c(tmle.est = 0.3), eic = rnorm(200, sd = 0.1)) calibrated_fit <- list(estimate = c(target.est = 0.5), eic = rnorm(200, sd = 0.1))  calibrated_contrasts(treatment_fit, placebo_fit, calibrated_fit) #>      contrast estimate         se     lower     upper #>        <char>    <num>      <num>     <num>     <num> #> 1:      total      0.4 0.01028048 0.3798506 0.4201494 #> 2:   mediated      0.2 0.01050568 0.1794092 0.2205908 #> 3: calibrated      0.2 0.01028145 0.1798487 0.2201513

title: Fit the initial hazard models — fit_initial
text: data data.frame observed event history data long format, one row per event columns id, time delta (integer code process jumped, 0 reserved censoring), plus baseline covariates used fit_types. fit_types named list one entry per event process, either model formula string list elements: model: formula string form "Surv(tstart, tstop, delta == k) ~ covariates", k process's delta code. processes can used covariates name, case counting process (lagged one event) used. fit: "cox" (default) "hal". at_risk: optional function data returning logical vector, marking rows risk process (e.g. function(dt) dt[["z"]] == 0 process can jump ). Exactly one process must delta code 0 (censoring). tau Positive number. Follow-horizon; target parameters evaluated tau. treatment_model Optional model baseline treatment A0, either formula string "A0 ~ L0" list elements model fit ("glm" supported). Required given. Optional integer vector baseline treatment values (0/1) compute interventional hazards clever weights . value can passed tmle_alpha(). max_count Positive integer. Maximum number jumps tracked per recurrent process state space. derived_vars Named list functions data deriving additional state variables. depend_time Named list functions describing dependence time since jump process, keyed process name. prune_states Logical. TRUE, prune states admissible at_risk functions fit_types. use_exponential Logical. TRUE, always transform hazard increments dH probabilities 1 - exp(-dH). Otherwise done increments exceed 1. hal_control named list settings processes fitted fit = "hal", see Details. cores Positive integer. Number cores used parallel::mclapply() predicting hazards across states. verbose Logical. TRUE, print model fits progress.

code: # psi(alpha) = 0.6 * (1 - exp(-alpha)) has a known inverse, so # solve_alpha() should recover alpha = -log(1 - 0.3 / 0.6). fun <- function(alpha) {   psi <- 0.6 * (1 - exp(-alpha))   list(estimate = c(tmle.est = psi, se = 0.01), eic = rep(0, 10)) } res <- solve_alpha(fun, theta = 0.3, c_n = 1e-6) res$alpha.hat #> [1] 0.6931482 -log(1 - 0.3 / 0.6) #> [1] 0.6931472
